text:
marta: Quick sync 19: re-evaluating the intake vs bench split for model onboarding. Goal: keep intake latency low while ensuring we don't promote bad models. Two decisions: what stays sync, what becomes async, and who is owner for alerts/artifacts?

aiden: Short answer: intake = lightning checks only. tokenizer compatibility, expected tensor shapes, tiny smoke generation (<=3 tokens), basic safety heuristics. Aim to keep intake < 300ms. Everything else moves to bench-runner async.

sam: Agree. Also propose a tiny validator service contract so intake can return immediate verdict + async reference. Sketch: POST /validators -> { quick_status: pass|warn|fail, job_id, telemetry_ref } then GET /validators/{job_id} -> { status, artifacts: [s3://...], metrics_id }.

jin: On telemetry: we need a canonical async result schema. Minimal fields: model_fingerprint, pipeline_version, latency_p50, latency_p95, tokens_per_sec, mem_peak_mb, golden_jsd, mismatch_rate, sample_count. Add submitter, onboard_id. Will also add recommended alert thresholds (p95 delta > 30% -> alert).

elsa: Ops concern: bench capacity. Full bench-per-model is costly. Suggest adaptive sampling: run full golden/quant checks for large models or new tokenizers, otherwise lightweight perf+quant smoke. Sampling config could be percent-based or rule-based (e.g., new tokenizer => 100%).

aiden: Example config I had in mind:```yaml
validation:
  fast_checks: [tokenizer, shape, smoke_generation, safety]
  async_checks: [perf_bench, quant_compat, golden_alignment]
  sampling:
    default_percent: 25
    rules:
      - when: new_tokenizer
        percent: 100
      - when: partner_whitelist
        percent: 100
  fast_accept_size_bytes: 131072
  canary_window_hours: 72
```

sam: Rollback question: If async bench later shows regression, do we auto-fallback? I vote for a conservative automatic fallback to last pinned stable model if p95 > baseline * 1.4 AND mismatch_rate > 0.15. Also open an incident to oncall. Manual override still possible.

marta: Ownership callout: intake API (devex) owns fast_checks and immediate verdicts; bench infra (eng-ml) owns async jobs, artifacts, metrics; runtime (eng-runtime) owns fallback hooks & pinned variants; deploy (eng-platform) owns canary promotion flow. We'll draft a 1-pager handoff.

ops-bot: Note: bench-runner maintenance 2026-06-10 02:00 UTC  expected 45m delay. Jobs queued during window may start late.

jin: I'll put together the telemetry JSON schema and sample Grafana/PromQL queries for p95 regressions. Will include example alert rule expressions.

elsa: +1 to the fallback policy. Also recommend a 24h "holding" period for auto-promote after canary passes to surface slow drift. Add a manual bypass flag for partners.

aiden: I'll estimate cost/slot-hours for a full async pass and propose a quota for self-serve vs partner-submitted models. Also will prototype a cheap pre-filter that rejects obvious quant-incompatible binaries before bench runs.

sam: I'll write the validator API RFC with error codes, rate limits, and example client flows. Will link in this thread when done.

marta: Action list: jin -> telemetry + alerts; sam -> validator API RFC; aiden -> bench cost + pre-filter prototype; elsa -> ops constraints + canary holding rules; marta -> handoff doc + consolidate config. I'll post a follow-up with the proposed YAML and timeline by EOD tomorrow. Thanks.
